Petforu POWKIDDY RGB10 MAX 2 Handheld Games Console 5-inch (17000 Games 128G Black) … this device came with no Charging Cable but that aside, how is the overall experience?

1. It feels “ok well” made and feels like its probably worth around 50-60$ in techology and material.
2. The screen resolution looks good
3. It says there is over 36000+ game on it.

Now lets get into the negative aspects:

1. Graphics: This emulator is VERY weak / has low processing power which makes “heavier” games basically unplayable/unenjoyable. (Framerate Drop, Audio Stretching, Gamespeed dropping)
2. Audio: The included audio speaker sounds like it is broken on my device and Mono only, which is alright, the issue is the games have been so compressed that most audio just sounds terrible.
3. Price: This device is too expensive for how it performs, it should be aroun 70-80$ max.

Conclusion:

I would Not recommend this emulator - if you are looking for a handheld gaming experience, you may want to look into a nintendo Switch or a Steam Deck.

Toysmith Kids Garden Tall Tool Set My son loves his "big boy" tools that I bought because he always wants to help me with yard work. I'm pretty disappointed with the build quality though. After teaching him how to rake up weeds, the head of the red rake was already starting to feel loose. We still have some snow on the ground here in Alaska so he tried to rake some snow and bent the rake when it hit a little ice. These are wood-handled metal tools, so I thought they would be more durable. For our application, I suppose I should have just bought him the little tools from Home Depot, but I figured I'd give these a shot for the price differential. Once again, the old adage proves true: you get what you pay for.

These tools would likely work well for sandbox or beach play, but they are certainly not made for actual work; even when the "worker" is a slightly undersized four-year-old. My recommendation would be to evaluate your intended use. If you've got an ambitious little guy or gal that wants to help out with yard work, pass on this set.

LEGO DUPLO My First Tow Truck 10918 Educational Tow Truck Toy, Great Gift for Kids Ages 18 Months and up, New 2020 (6 Pieces) Because I love all LEGO building kits for heavy construction equipment (e.g., [[ASIN:B07Y8T4WHC LEGO Mobile Crane]]), I couldn’t resist this cute little LEGO DUPLO MY FIRST TOW TRUCK 10918 (New 2020 (6 Pieces)). It’s absolutely charming, all 6 pieces of it!

I really like the drivers’ windows, with a boy on one side and a girl on the other. It makes this into a truly unisex toy. I love the big blue traffic cone that fits between the drivers’ cabin and the moveable crane for transport. Tow trucks always set out traffic cones, for safety, when they’re readying a tow. The crane itself is fun because it swings up and down freely.

The building instructions are on the outside of the retail box. The toy takes about 30 seconds for an adult to assemble, as the wheels are already attached to the truck base. When the toy is finished, it makes a terrific truck for general play. The wheels turn freely, and the truck feels solid and satisfying when it’s pushed around.

Inside the box is a printed city street layout. The paper is very thin, so this won’t last long unless it’s glued to some sort of heavier backing. However the street layout fits the assembled tow truck, and is a nice detail.

Note that this is a LEGO duplo model, intended for very young children. The pieces are much larger than standard LEGO pieces. They are compatible with other duplo building sets, but NOT with standard LEGO elements.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO DUPLO My First Tow Truck 10918 Educational Tow Truck Toy, Great Gift for Kids Ages 18 Months and up, New 2020 (6 Pieces)

text_fidelity_a:
Pandasaurus Games Sonora - Unique Family-Friendly Board Games, for Adults, Teens & Kids (2-4 Players) , Orange This is a simple "flick-and-write" game with good production values, a questionable rulebook, simple and fast gameplay, and a box that is just ridiculously large for what it is.

Gameplay is fast and straightforward, involving a Crokinole style mechanism for shooting your disc into a recessed game board with a central hole in the middle. This board has a plastic shelf with corner sections for "shooting" pieces, and they'll fall into a central area divided into four main sections. My central board easily comes loose from the shelving piece, and needs to be adjusted prior to gameplay almost all the time. Once you shoot, you'll be making marks onto your player board with the included markers, which are of average quality for a game like this. The boards are easily erasable - a major plus to the production aspect of the game.

The rules are not that hard, but they are explained in a way that makes learning the game quite a bit more difficult than it needs to be. Few examples are covered, and there will be a number of times that you run into situations where you aren't sure how to interpret the rule as written. Once you get it though, play is not too hard, and Sonora is something you can play with the kids after you've worked out the kinks. And they'll want to play this - it's colorful, with kid-friendly artwork, and the gameplay looks like a kid's game, but has enough meat to interest an adult for at least a little while. I don't know that I'd play this game too often, but it is certainly different and a good family game that will keep kids interested. You can play a few games back to back, as they'll run 20 minutes or so once you know the general flow of the game. For a family game night, this will be a good alternative to a more traditional strategy or roll-and-move board game.

The biggest downfall of this one is that the box is so large. As a gamer with a large collection, it's disappointing to see a 12x12 "Ticket to Ride" sized box for a game that could have opted for a foldable game board and fit into a very small game box. They would have lost nothing in doing this, and in fact, they might have fixed the issue I have with the main board. Even if they must have a one-piece board, dropping the molded plastic insert that holds a handful of discs and pens could have reduced the size by a few inches in depth. In reality, there's not much here in the box, and the components can be entirely stored in the recessed game board area alone. That would be about 3/4" in depth, not 3".

All in all, it's OK.
text_fidelity_b: Pandasaurus Games Sonora - Unique Family-Friendly Board Games, for Adults, Teens & Kids (2-4 Players) , Orange

text_fidelity_a:
Hot Wheels Track Builder Triple Loop Stunt Loops Hot Wheels 1:64 scale Vehicles [[VIDEOID:886df78722d87a8bdca79a9702180ce2]] This set is awesome!! There are a couple things to note about it that could be potential downsides/issues, if not prepared for-- but otherwise, everything is great! Below I will group the main points and for the 3 potential issues I'll mark it with this symbol:🔴 to hopefully make it easier to read through!

•We received all pieces included, and boxing, in great condition.

•1 car is included

•The quality of materials are true to Hot Wheels- great and sturdy plastic.

•It's a fairly easy set-up. My 9 year old put it together on her own by reading through the instructions step-by-step. It took around 30 minutes, may have been quicker but she often took short pauses, though she didn't need any help.

•There are about 3 different configurations you can do with this set. The video I posted shows each of these.

•Can connect to other Hot Wheels tracks and sets. (Including the colossal crash set that can be seen some in the background of the video I posted)

•Does not require batteries

•There are no levers that need to be reset for cars to go through the loops- my daughter has other loop sets that have those.

•You can set it up so that the launcher connects and starts at any of the loops. For example- you can connect the launcher to just the middle loop and the smallest. You can also try to launch it opposite- starting at the smallest loop and ending with the largest.

•You don't have to use the jumping ramps…you can have the cars finish the loops on a flat track.

🔴 One of the potential issues is the launcher- maybe it's just our launcher, or how we use it, but it can be a bit tricky to hit it with the right amount of pressure. Too hard and it knocks it off track. Too soft and it won't go around the loop. Sometimes it can take many tries and others it works right away. We have a few other types of launchers-- the long white one that is shown in the video I posted is the one she prefers to use since it seems to work better. Not everyone will have extra launchers, though. My daughter usually has no problem with trying multiple times with the one included in the set but I figured it's worth noting that it may not be a perfect launch each time.

🔴 The other possible issue are the cars used with it. You'll likely want at least a handful of different types of cars on hand, just in case. The one included does work pretty good. My daughter has a decent sized collection of cars and there a quite a few that often don't make it through the biggest loop. This could either be the car itself that doesn't work well or could also be an issue of the launcher (as just mentioned above). Some of her cars struggle on the biggest loop with the launcher provided- but when connected to the "stronger" launcher, they do great. And there's a few that still just don't make it. This could be an issue if this were very first set for a kiddo and if they have only 1 or 2 cars…just something to keep in mind if considering purchasing this set, you may want to consider also purchasing a handful of cars so that they can get the most use from it.

🔴 When you have it set-up as the Daredevil Jump or Gravity Drop, it sort of seems like the track isn't long enough since the cars shoot further past the cup a lot. So we added extra tracks (which aren't included in this set) and it helped a lot…the cars land in the cup more times than not. At the very end of the video I posted, you can see how we added an extra track to the Daredevil Jump set-up.

All-in-all: We love it! It keeps my 9 year old busy-- even if she doesn't connect it to her other tracks. She likes trying to get the cars in the cup and thinks that the triple loop feature is awesome.
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Track Builder Triple Loop Stunt Loops Hot Wheels 1:64 scale Vehicles

The box, however, doesn’t let you see the colored bit on the bottom of the pencil, so it is really difficult to tell the color while using the box. The colors are also pretty off from the color on the bottom. Thee re hexagon shaped, so they won’t roll away from you. The actual pencil “lead” seems exactly the same as standard Crayola colored pencils. I compared them side by side and they color the same. They both have fairly soft “lead”. These are sharpened better in their presharpened state. The standard Crayola colored pencil also appear to have a bit of a chalky residue on the “lead” and these don’t, but I didn’t find that to change how they function in any way. These look a little more high end, but color pretty much the same as a Crayola colored pencil. These don’t feel like fine art quality, just hobby/craft quality. They are good for adult coloring books, which is what I got them for, so I’m happy with them. They just aren’t the quality of higher end colored pencils as they are packaged to have you believe.

Ravensburger Zodiac 270 Piece Puzzle Ball Unlike traditional jigsaw puzzles, the pieces are made of hard plastic rather than cardboard or foam, which means it's more durable. I remember growing up with jigsaw puzzles where the pictures got chipped because the paper would peel off the cardboard. The colors are bright, shiny and very decorative. Also unlike cardboard jigsaws, the pieces actually stay together and the ball can be held up when finished. Very cool.

On the negative side, I don't like the fact that the pieces are numbered on the back. For me, this takes away the challenge of being detail-oriented and noticing the tiny details that make one piece go with another. It feels like a dumbing-down to me. I could see the numbered sequence being good for younger kids, but not for something that's geared to 10 and older.

Other than that, this is a high quality, solidly made puzzle that families would enjoy doing together.

WHAT ARE THESE LIKE?
This package comes with two bags of pens. There are two of each color in each bag for a total of 4 each color:
Black
Red
Neon Green
Yellow
Purple

Neon Pink

The caps each have a light in them with a paper tab to remove when it is time to use one. The top has a little light in it that if you press a button on the side, the light goes on. The pen itself is white like a marker type.

DO THESE WORK UNDER BLACKLIGHT?
Yes, if you were to decorate something that you plan to have in a blacklight room (halloween, lessons, parties, etc), the writing will show up when the blacklights come on. It would be great for a mystery theater too.

HOW POPULAR WERE THESE?
The kids LOVE these. It keeps them busy for a little while anyway. They also made a nice prize for games.

THE BOTTOM LINE
A great item to have on hand for a variety of reasons- from kids and parties, to mystery theaters, these markers are delightful. I love the colors they come in too- the writing is all the same, just the outside is different.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS! I personally love to play with these as much as all of the kids do!

My favorite feature is the bomb hatch located behind the pilot/passenger compartment that seats the minifigs. You can seat Spidey in the hatch, press a button, and let him drop down on his web string to dangle beneath the plane. You can also use the hatch to drop brick-built energy bombs. The jet has a minimum of stickers (always a good thing, in my opinion). The “adjustable wings” are the two upper ones at the tail. They can be adjusted to different angles. The big wings at the sides, and their wingtips, are fixed in place.

The kit includes minifigs for Happy Hogan, Nick Fury, Spider-Man, and Mysterio, as well as their associated weapons.

Bézier Games Ultimate Werewolf Revised Edition Werewolf is not usually a "game night" game that you play with a group of friends. I've always used it in classroom settings, or with larger groups, usually upwards of 10 people, where this game really shines. Ultimately, Werewolf is a deduction game in which most players are Villagers, unwittingly being killed or eliminated by a sect of Werewolf players. Using very limited clues and knowledge, it's up to the Villagers to unmask the Werewolves and eliminate them from the game before they themselves are eaten.

The only real issue that I have with Werewolf is that there is player elimination, although since Werewolf is not a particularly long game, it's usually OK, and bystanders often have as much fun as the players.

There are plenty of versions of this game available out there, but I think that Bezier's "Ultimate" is certainly the way to go. The bits are durable and well made, and there are enough cards to play an 80 person game. That said, there is less content in here as compared to the "Revised Edition" that came out a few years ago. I still think that this is the box to get, however, as the roles and unique playing styles presented in the "Revised" box are more complicated, and not really in line with the casual spirit of the game. I think they certainly provide more variety, but at the expense of complicating the players and making it far more difficult for the moderator. As it's impossible to answer questions mid-game, it's best to leave the complicated roles to a different genre of game.

A 5-Star Product for sure.
text_fidelity_b: Bézier Games Ultimate Werewolf Revised Edition

+Has very informative information about each country
+You can stick the magnets to your fridge, too
+Extremely excellent packaging
+Very high quality wood backing

Cons:
-The magnets aren't very strong, so you'll be rearranging them a lot

LEGO The Movie 2 Pop-Up Party Bus 70828 Building Kit, Build Your Own Toy Party Bus for 9+ Year Old Girls and Boys (1013 Pieces) (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I really enjoyed the Lego movie Lego kits, because they just add so much color, costuming and fun to normal building. The mini figures are much more like the Lego friends than like the normal ones, and the pink Afro, unicorn Kitty, robot, etc. added a lot of fun to the build process to have those as accessories.

My son at six has done hundreds of Lego sets because we are a homeschooling family and incorporate that into our curriculum. This build took him a few days of intermittent building and he felt enthusiastic and excited about the set and kept discovering cool new features and decorative accents to how it worked. The little light up brick inside was a really fun touch, also.

Once the bus is constructed, it has a little more play value than some of the other Lego vehicles and sets that we have built. So many toys once constructed seem to explode apart with the most gentle of play, while this party bus is built pretty sturdy. We've had a number of young friends visit and want to play with it, and while a few little pieces of broken off, it was in the realm of being very easy to repair rather than having major structural problems upon actual children actually playing with it.

Overall this is a really fun set, a fun build that is fairly straightforward, and results in a sturdy toy at the end. Little sister was particularly taken with the accessories.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO The Movie 2 Pop-Up Party Bus 70828 Building Kit, Build Your Own Toy Party Bus for 9+ Year Old Girls and Boys (1013 Pieces) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
Melissa & Doug Created by Me! Owl Pillow, 6+ years Here are some observations from my wife.

My almost-5-year-old daughter LOVES this owl pillow craft project, and so do I! She and I have just begun working on sewing with a needle and thread, but I must be sure to be with her every minute, with my hands along with hers on our first sewing projects. This pillow, however, is so smartly designed that it allows her the freedom to practice sewing buttons ON HER OWN, and she loves that freedom. I can be close to her, at the sink, putting away dishes, while she creates her pillow all by herself. It’s a big deal to her. : )

I definitely had to sit with her at the start to go through the simple instructions and to get her started on the process. She enjoyed choosing her own pattern for the owl and decided to choose the same pattern as the owl of the adorable girl on the box. I showed her how to do the first few stitches, and then she was off and running. Once she got going on her own, she kept saying, “This is so easy! This is so fun!” while working on stitching through the felt buttons.

After our first hour on the project today, she’s definitely getting the hang of the process, and she can work on it on her own with me close by for the occasional help with knotting off a thread. And though she really wanted to be able to sleep with the pillow tonight, she’s excited to spend more time stitching the felt buttons onto her owl over the coming days. I’m glad that the project will take 5-7 days of stitching for her to complete. It’s longer than just an hour or even one-day project for her, since she’s at the young side of the recommended age range (6-10 years old). It’s possible an older child could finish this project in a few hours of an afternoon.

And I have to say that I’m thrilled that it’s machine washable. Overall, this is a fantastic and adorable craft for a little one at the very beginning stages of learning to sew.
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Created by Me! Owl Pillow, 6+ years

text_fidelity_a:
LiangCuber Tornado V3 M Flagship Speed Cube QY Toys X Man Tornado V3 Magnetic 3x3 Cube (Tornado V3 M Magnetic Core Flagship) When I got this, I still didn't solve the Rubik's cube. I know there are all kinds of tutorials, but I wanted to solve it on my own. Fast-forward 11 years later, I flipped the table (so to speak) and watched a couple tutorials. This was the cube I used to solve the puzzle for the first time. I watched a couple videos of the cube before receiving mine to get a better understanding of the mechanisms and design. During my first session, I set the magnets to the strongest and left the dials as they were. Two hours is how long it took me to solve it on the first try.

I like that this cube comes with a handful of accessories. I use the case to carry the cube with me to and from work. It stays on my desk; whenever I have to read something on my monitors and not use the keyboard, I solve a little bit. Now I can solve the cube in minutes, though it took me a few days to get to this point. I now have the spring and tension set to the strongest for how much force can be pulled and weakest for how fast turns can be. (Apologies for not using the correct terms, but I tried looking up what the dials exactly do and I still can't figure out which does what with regard to the terminology, but I base it off feel.)

The cube comes with a leather bag and a tool to adjust the magnets. The first time I accessed the dials, I used a pen to pop off the tiles. They can be difficult to pull off by hand alone, even after being pulled so many times. The lever for each dial also was difficult to pull. Now, I leave it semi-flush to the dial to make it easier to access in the future. They also pop off easily, but are [somewhat] easy to put back. The magnet levels sometimes move on their own. If I happen to notice a magnet at a strength I didn't set it at, I'll re-adjust. Annoying, but an easy fix. I no longer use the tool that came with the cube because any item small and flat enough will work. The bag is kept in the box for now.

There are two manuals that come with the cube: one for the cube itself and the other on how to solve it. I tried using the solve tutorial but found it confusing with some typographical errors, so I used videos. I learn better visually anyway. Even though the cube's manual has great illustrations for the mechanics, I failed to understand what they actually do, so I looked up videos for that too.

This is the third cube I own and currently it's my favorite. Each time my time lowers after solving, I adjust the settings. I'm becoming a speedcuber without realizing it.
text_fidelity_b: LiangCuber Tornado V3 M Flagship Speed Cube QY Toys X Man Tornado V3 Magnetic 3x3 Cube (Tornado V3 M Magnetic Core Flagship)

That, coupled with the fact we have a cat; the basketballs remain exposed, and the cat loves to play.

LEGO Star Wars Millennium Falcon Microfighter 75193 Building Kit (92 Pieces) If you have a 6 year old who is into Star Wars and who also loves Legos (or maybe you would like to get them into Legos and/or Star Wars), then this is a great Lego kit to do just that. I bought this and the one with the bad guy for my son's Easter Basket. Being a "connoisseur" of Star Wars and Legos, my son lost his mind when he saw what the Easter Bunny brought.

The Lego Microfighters are mini vehicles you build, which you can use to either expand your Lego-verse or play with separately. These come with instructions on how to build the microfighter. They are simple to put together, but I would not advise this for a child younger than 6 unless you know your 4 or 5 year old is really good at Lego instructions (which are in picture form). These are not ideal for children who are still primarily freebuilders or just learning about Legos. You should get the creative set for that. However, if your child loves to freebuild, but can also follow instructions this is a great gift! My son built all of the microfighters as designed, played with them for a bit, and then rearranged them to his freebuilding heart's desire. I cut the instructions apart and rearrange them in plastic sleeves so that if he wants to build according to the instructions they are neat and organized. Also do not let the "Micro" fool you, they are regular sized Legos, they will work with other Legos, it's just that they are really small scaled models. Also, the Lego people (Chewbacca) that come the sets are regular sized Lego people. So, their body parts can be mixed and matched with others you have in your collection.

One Caveat: For some odd reason, these sets as well as some of the smaller Lego City sets always have their boxes just crushed and in horrible shape. So, if you are looking for these are gift, I usually purchase from a store like Target, Walmart, or the Lego store itself to pick out the very best box. I'm not sure why Lego does this. I used to blame Target, but then I realized this was a Lego issue and not a store issue.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Star Wars Millennium Falcon Microfighter 75193 Building Kit (92 Pieces)

Crayola Glow Book Seeing commercials for the Glow Book, I've been interested in this toy for my 9 year old. Obviously commercials are made to show the absolute best of a product, so I expected it to be much less than what was advertised. I have to admit it's almost as cool as the advertisements. However, the best way to discover if a toy is really worth it is to test it out on more than just a few kids. I went with those who were interested in art. Thus, this is judging based on kids who are already fans of art.

Honest opinions from kids:

1. It came with pages you could trace for kids who can't draw too well.
2. If you make a mistake, it's easy to erase it, but it's hard to make it all clean. You really have to rub well to erase mistakes or it leaves smearing behind. They should have something to erase it better. At least you can use it more than one time.
3. It needs more pages. You have plastic pages you draw on and the lights come on to show each page. It makes everything look like it's moving when the lights flash. The pages also aren't very straight.
4. I really like to play with the glow book because it is fun. You just have to get used to using it.
5. It was just like a movie. I could color and draw it just how I pleased.
6. It would be nice if there could be just a little more colors because it shows purple in some of the tracings, but there is no purple. Maybe some black to show outlines, too. It just comes with six colors: tan, pink, yellow, blue, red and green.

From an adult's perspective - it definitely has keep the interest going with the kids. It's not a toy that ends up on the shelf - lost and forgotten. However, the price tag is a bit high for something that's so simple. I have seen Amazon have excellent deals on the Glow Book, however, and think if you are patient and give yourself time to find a great deal, you will. Anything less than $20 would be great. I agree with one of the children that it could use more colors. Especially when dealing with kids interested in art. For younger kids, the small amount of color choices is probably fine. Glass cleaner takes care of the smudges you'll find after repeated use by kids. After a few mistakes, the drawing takes on a foggy/dusty look - thus making it harder to see the pictures "move" clearly. Downside is it can't be cleaned until the child is entirely finished. Definitely stick with the manufacturer age recommendation of 6 years and up. This toy is not made well enough to handle rough use from younger kids.

MAGICYOYO Responsive Yoyo V3, Professional Metal Yoyo for Kids Beginner, Aluminum Alloy Yoyo with Unresponsive Bearing + Bearing Removal Tool + Axle + Bag + 12 Yoyo Strings (Black Blue Purple) There was one summer in the very end of the 90s that I got into yo-yos. They boomed at my elementary school--so much so that eventually they were banned. After that ban, I wanted to see the fuss. I didn't get into them right away because many of my classmates were learning more advanced tricks by the time I realized the hype, and I figured I'd never get to that level. But during one fateful summer, away from the city for the whole season, I practiced on my own. I learned a few tricks, but that was it.

I did some research to see where I left off (quite a lot has happened), and looked up beginner-friendly yo-yos. I ordered this one and it's been played with daily since it arrived. It's very easy to use for someone like me who hasn't touched one in 20 years. There are different strings available, so no need to stress on back-ups just yet. There is also a bearing for an unresponsive mod, but I'm not there yet. So far, I've been able to re-do most of the tricks I learned, and I'm happy to see what else I'll learn with this one.

2058 Pieces City Police Mobile Command Truck Toy Building Blocks Set for Kids, Boys Age 6+, with Police Station, Police Cars, Airplane, Helicopter, Boat, 2022 Newest Police Toy Gift for Police Fans This is one of the better kits that this brand makes. They're compatible with LEGO, albeit of a lower quality overall, and this is another of their designs that don't come with minifigs, and which isn't inherently designed for them. You'll make model police vehicles, but your LEGO dudes won't go riding around in them - they simply won't fit.

The other big downside is that you don't get to do the bags in order like you do with LEGO. You kind of have to open them all at once and work from one gigantic pile in the center of the table. It's messy and can lead to quitting, but that's all part of the experience.

They will fit somewhat within the tractor component, which is the largest piece of this set, and by far the most interesting. There are a number of playable aspects to this that give you a lot more bang for your buck than the more model-focused kits we've tried from Wishalife previously.

Overall, there's plenty of bricks, OK instructions, a large number of stickers, and plenty of fun to be had here. No, it's not LEGO, but it's not too bad considering. This is a great buy to keep your kids playing for some time.
text_fidelity_b: 2058 Pieces City Police Mobile Command Truck Toy Building Blocks Set for Kids, Boys Age 6+, with Police Station, Police Cars, Airplane, Helicopter, Boat, 2022 Newest Police Toy Gift for Police Fans

Faber-Castell How to Rainbow Watercolor Pencils Set - Kids Painting Kits, Art Kit for Kids 6-8+ At the time of this review, this set is under $10. If it were over $10, I would probably subtract a star. This is definitely beginner, student quality.
But if you have a child, or maybe you are just looking for something reasonably priced to see if you enjoy sketching, even though it's geared for children, this set can't be beat.

The main reason it gets five stars, is that you get four different hardness levels of graphite pencils. Perfect for experimenting with your creativity and making a sketch come alive. And it's less messy than charcoal sticks, so once again, it's the perfect introduction to nurture a child's creativity and talent.
To make it even better, there's a little pamphlet to encourage and explain how to get your feet wet. I really like that the emphasis is on the fact that there are no mistakes, that each line is is just fine. So important for children that might be discouraged that they aren't instantly a great artist, forgetting or not understanding that being an artist is only 10% talent and 90% learning and desire.
It might be only a folded over page, but it covers various techniques. All is written in a way that kids and young adults can easily follow. This set is cured for ages 7 and up.
And once again, a 7-year-old doesn't need professional quality pencil sharpeners or paper. You can see in the photograph how thin the paper pages are, and how cheesy the little pencil sharpener is. Cheesy, but perfect for the purpose.

This well thought out set is just what I would expect from Farber-Castell. Their supplies are favored by the students and professionals worldwide.

I hope that this review has helped you to make a decision about whether or not this set is right for you or a special child. Kids seem to be passionate about something one minute, and totally change the next. This little set is a very small investment, but of course, little investments add up.

xxoo

Assassin’s Creed Syndicate Assassin's Gauntlet with Hidden Blade This is so much nicer than the cane sword. It fits on the left hand and the blade ejects with a snick kind of sound, and quite a bit of force. It's spring loaded, and if you look very closely you can see the spring, but I could imagine the "original" was the same. It's heavy leather and has gorgeous detailing. This one is worthy of Comicon or serious cos play.

The "metal" looks aged aged, a little oxidized, and not at all like plastic. It barely feels like plastic when you run your fingers over it, only a bit too warm in the cold weather. The leather looks distressed, and a bit worn, even on the inside by the knuckles. The stitching in the leather is impeccable, and with a great eye for detail. Some of the stitches are a tad longer than others, which happens with hand sewing, not typically with machine stitching. Yes, it was clearly done by machine, but the effect is to look pre-industrial which fits the game perfectly. There is even fake dirt in the spring of the grapple line.

The buckles on top are non-functional. It stays on with velcro straps on the bottom. It fits my small woman hands only barely and I imagine would be fine on a fairly tall man as well.

As with the cane, this is not for kids. The blade is on the sharp side, as is the assassin logo grapple point (I didn't notice in the game that the hook is the logo -- very cool detail). It could do some damage, especially if pointed to the eyes, and the grapple hook is a bit delicate looking. Nothing serious, but handle with some care.

Insect Lore - Butterfly Growing Kit - Butterfly Habitat Kit with Voucher to Redeem 5 Caterpillars, STEM Journal, Butterfly Feeder & More – Life Science & STEM Education – Butterfly Science Kit The Live Butterfly Garden by Insect Lore is a fun, hands- on educational experience that is certain to appeal to even the most stubborn, disinterested child. With the Live Butterfly Garden, children get to observe the process of metamorphosis, right before their eyes. Starting with caterpillars, children watch the little critters eat food, create a cocoon, and then transform into fully grown adult butterflies. The butterflies can then be observed in their habitat for a while before setting free.

This butterfly garden is great for dozens of reasons, the most obvious of which is the educational value. Reading about insects and metamorphosis is one thing, but seeing the process live is another thing entirely. Kids get to learn how caterpillars/butterflies live, eat, and thrive; how to care for them; etc. They get to observe the caterpillars and butterflies at play and watch the butterflies eat their food, which is provided in the package. The caterpillars that come with the Live Butterfly Garden are painted ladies, which are not very common and will not be recognized by most children. However, most kids won't care- the fun of watching these small caterpillars transform into butterflies will have many kids gazing in awe, and prompt them to ask many questions.

This educational toy is a huge hit and my kids loved it, but there were a few small issues. One was waiting for the caterpillars to arrive in the mail. To get the caterpillars, you have to mail in an included certificate, along with a check, and then wait. It seems like an eternity, especially from the perspective of young children, and it took longer than expected. Anther problem was parting with the butterflies. Once you have the caterpillars and they have transformed into adult butterflies, the next problem will be setting them free. Kids will grow attached to their small, winged friends and will not want to let them go. Another minor issue is with the transferring of the caterpillars from their small container- the one you receive in the mail- into the actual habitat. The container that the caterpillars arrive in has a paper area at the top, where the caterpillars will hang as they spin their cocoons. This paper section is fairly easy to remove, but the problem is that the cocoons are very delicately attached, and that means that some will fall off when the transfer is made. You will need to pin this piece of paper to the inside of the butterfly garden, but the kit doesn't include any pins. Safety pins or straight pins work, and it would have been nice if these were included in the kit.

Still, when all factors are considered, the Live Butterfly Garden is worth the purchase and young children will enjoy the educational experience. Sure, it could be improved a little bit by making a few minor changes, but this is still a very good toy and considering my kid's fascination with the process, along with the educational value, it earns an easy recommendation.
text_fidelity_b: Insect Lore - Butterfly Growing Kit - Butterfly Habitat Kit with Voucher to Redeem 5 Caterpillars, STEM Journal, Butterfly Feeder & More – Life Science & STEM Education – Butterfly Science Kit

text_fidelity_a:
Treasure X Quest for Dragons Gold - Deluxe Dragon Figure My six-year-old just love sitting down for an hour or more, chipping away at the block of chalk with all of the little toy parts inside. As he finds each part, he sprays it off with the little spray bottle of water that I provide him while he plays, and at the end he and his father put the toy together. While my son is very good at building with Legos, these don't go together as gracefully as Legos do, so little adult assistance with the assembly is necessary.

When my son gets in a certain mood where he's having trouble focusing on more intellectual activities, this is a great way of focusing some of his nervous energy and allowing him to re-center himself. It definitely feels like a much requested and beloved event when I bring one of these out.
text_fidelity_b: Treasure X Quest for Dragons Gold - Deluxe Dragon Figure

text_fidelity_a:
ROKR 3D Wooden Puzzles for Adults Illuminated Globe with Stand 180pcs 3D Puzzles Built-in LED Model Kit Hobby Gifts for Adults/Teens Home Decor I was super excited to receive this item because it claims to light up and turn in multiple ways, however assembly was a pain! Assembly of this product was so painstaking, I ended up having a couple of dented finger nails, some splinters, and a bunch of broken and scratched up skin. This item requires a lot of finger strength, yet it requires gentle assembly. There are certain parts during assembly where it requires me to gently slide in one part, yet push it in with force. the longitudinal wood pieces came in 12 pieces, but to assemble, it must fit into 5 different slots. I broke about 9 little slots in 9 difference pieces. The instructions were all pictures, but certain parts of the instruction must be studied in detail!!! I studied certain steps and was confident; turned out, I was wrong and had to break it apart which caused more broken wooden pieces. The last part, one of the pieces didn't come fully cut, so when I pushed a piece in, it snapped. Overall, if this item I assembled was not examined in detail, nobody would see any of the cracks. I like what I assembled and it did turn out great, but I refuse to ever do this again!

and it wont turn! I waxed the pieces that required waxing, but as hard as I try to turn the knobs, the globe wont turn! If I force, it'll turn a little bit, but I feel like it might break!
text_fidelity_b: ROKR 3D Wooden Puzzles for Adults Illuminated Globe with Stand 180pcs 3D Puzzles Built-in LED Model Kit Hobby Gifts for Adults/Teens Home Decor
